name: supervised_anchor_v1 (stage 1 of the supervised/calibrated work plan, 2026-11-01)
frozen_at: 2026-11-01, written before any score of the new arms was computed
origin: Bracha Laufer (emails 2026-10-23, 2026-10-29): use labelled data to find the weighting instead of label-free weights. Follow-up to bracha_lr_transfer_v1. Approved by Omri 2026-11-01 ('Yes, start stage 1').
question: If the telemetry direction stays the label-free L-SML one and labels learn only the PRM-vs-telemetry mixing ratio (2 coefficients), does this beat (i) label-free AUTO, (ii) the PRM alone, and (iii) a full 17-input supervised LR trained on the same labels? Especially: does it give a strong PRM its due weight on Socratic?
access: CPU only, stored per-step scores, no new inference. Every new arm uses correctness labels and is labelled supervised.

benchmarks.hard2verify: secondary, evaluated on the 177-answer common set (stage8 eval_rows); never a training source

inputs.zp: answer-z of the PRM risk (PRM_Q80 on PRMBench, PRM elsewhere), as AUTO and stage8
inputs.zT16: answer-z of the stored label-free TELE_N16 score (L-SML over the 16 backbone channels)
inputs.zS5: answer-z of the stored label-free TELE_S5 score (SUB5)
inputs.Z16: answer-z of the 16 backbone channels (E.channels N16)

arms.AUTO_N16: label-free L-SML on [zp, Z16]; recomputed with stage8 auto() and parity-checked
arms.ANCH_T16: LR on [zp, zT16]: label-free telemetry direction, learned PRM/telemetry ratio
arms.LR17: LR on [zp, Z16]: full supervised weighting (CROP-style)

model: StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(l2, class_weight balanced, lbfgs, max_iter 3000); C in {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10} by inner GroupKFold(5) on the training rows only, criterion mean held-out pooled step AUROC (same as bracha_lr_transfer_v1); refit on all training rows. Score = decision_function.

regimes.IN: in-domain cross-fit: GroupKFold(5) over the benchmark's source groups (c.groups); each answer is scored by a model that never saw its group. PRMBench and Socratic only.
regimes.XFER: trained once on all of one benchmark, applied unchanged to another, same PRM: prmbench->socratic, prmbench->hard2verify, socratic->prmbench, socratic->hard2verify

training_rows: PRMBench: steps with c.keep (non-control answers); Socratic: all steps
decision_rule: GAP for every arm (stage7 gap_flags), as in stage8
metrics: main metric under GAP (PRMBench/Socratic PRMScore, Hard2Verify balanced F1; stage8 point())
learned PRM share |w_zp| / sum|w| on standardized inputs
uncertainty: paired bootstrap with evaluate_collection boot_weights (source groups; DRAWS 2000), stage8 boot(): delta and 95% CI on both metrics

predeclared_readings.H1: IN, PRMBench: ANCH_T16 - AUTO_N16 main-metric CI above 0 in >= 3 of 4 PRMs
predeclared_readings.H2: IN, Socratic: ANCH_T16 - PRM main-metric CI above 0 in >= 3 of 4 PRMs (the strong-PRM problem)
predeclared_readings.H3: XFER prmbench->socratic: ANCH_T16 - LR17 main metric > 0 (point) in >= 3 of 4 PRMs (fewer learned parameters transfer better)
predeclared_readings.note: Readings, not pass/fail gates for a method; all results are reported per PRM x benchmark regardless.

parity_first: AUTO_N16 gap_prmscore and within_auc must reproduce stage8/AUTO_FORCEDK_RESULTS.json to 1e-6 in every cell before any new arm is reported
caveats: All three benchmarks are development data already inspected; no untouched confirmation.
Problem overlap between PRMBench and Socratic cannot be checked offline (no Socratic problem text); XFER may be optimistic if they share source problems.

amendments.change: ANCH_S5 and TELE_S5 removed, with their contrasts.
amendments.why: TELE_S5 is stored only for PRMBench cells (not Socratic/Hard2Verify), and a direct L-SML rebuild over the six SUB5 channels does not reproduce the stored PRMBench score (r=.83). The first run stopped with KeyError before parity; no new-arm score was computed.
